_transcription: COMPLETE — all five sections, 52 rows. The paper is bilingual on alternating pages and the alternating hypothesis HELD: idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English General Instructions + Q1-Q3, and every EVEN index 2..22 is English (its odd predecessor is the Hindi of the same block). English pages used: 2 (Q1-3), 4 (Q4-9), 6 (Q10-14), 8 (Q15-18 + the Assertion-Reason instruction block), 10 (Q19-21), 12 (Q22-26), 14 (Q27-31), 16 (Q32-35), 18 (Case Study - 1 / Q36), 20 (Case Study - 2 / Q37), 22 (Case Study - 3 / Q38). Every MCQ answer is the official marking scheme's 'Ans' row, verbatim; the 15 shared with 65/1/1 all agree with that paper's recorded key. REUSE: 39 of the 52 rows are the same printed block as 65/1/1 under DIFFERENT question numbers (this paper's Q3 is 65/1/1's Q15, its Q8 is their Q2, its whole Section E is their Section E permuted: CS-1 here is their CS-3, CS-2 here is their CS-1, CS-3 here is their CS-2). Each was confirmed on this paper's own page and then reused byte-for-byte from data/2024-65-1-1.questions.json, verified programmatically as 39/39 identical in stem, context, options, answer and taxonomy. Genuinely NEW to this set: Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7, Q12 (MCQs), Q22(a), Q22(b), Q23, Q26, Q31, Q32, Q34(a), Q34(b). Option labels are printed (A) (B) (C) (D), upper case, and stored upper case. Q6 prints the transpose marks as typographic primes (A′B′); stored as ASCII apostrophes to match the bank's existing convention (65/1/1 Q11 stores P(A')). The printed 'Case Study - N' headings use an EN DASH and are recorded in _caseStudyLabel, never in context. FIGURES: the 2024 question-paper renders black out the lower half of Q21's parallelogram figure on page idx 10, but the marking scheme (ms page idx 7) reproduces the same figure legibly — it is a plain labelled parallelogram ABCD with diagonal DB and no measurements, so nothing is read off it (AD follows algebraically from the two printed vectors) and no figure is attached, matching 65/1/1's treatment of the same block. Q26 is an LPP but states every constraint in text and expects the student to DRAW the region, so it carries no figure dependency either.

questions.context:
According to recent research, air turbulence has increased in various regions around the world due to climate change. Turbulence makes flights bumpy and often delays the flights.

Assume that, an airplane observes severe turbulence, moderate turbulence or light turbulence with equal probabilities. Further, the chance of an airplane reaching late to the destination are 55%, 37% and 17% due to severe, moderate and light turbulence respectively.

On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Find the probability that an airplane reached its destination late.
